Aurora Intelligence

Intelligence on your terms. Not a corporate subscription.

Instead of fifty separate desktop applications running heavy background LLMs and burning gigabytes of RAM, Aurora provides a unified, secure system service that applications use with your explicit permission.

Security Invariants

Zero ambient authority. Built from the ground up.

Applications never receive automatic system-wide surveillance powers. Every capability requires an explicit, cryptographically checked token. If an action isn't permitted, the request fails closed in microseconds.

Unified Service

AI that assists. Never insists.

Aurora OS re-engineers how applications communicate with intelligence. By centralizing reasoning into an OS-level service, your computer stays quiet, fast, and unified.

  • Unified system service: Applications share a single, optimized intelligence provider.
  • Pluggable model backends: Use local neural weights or tiny fast SLMs without rewriting apps.
  • Predictable resilience: If an AI model stalls, the Linux desktop never crashes.

// Aurora IPC Flow (ADR-001)

Applications ──(D-Bus)──▶ aurora-ai daemon

↳ WorkerSupervisor (Rust)

↳ CapabilityDispatcher & PolicyEngine

↳ Local Inference Engine

↳ Linux Kernel Substratum

Strict Confinement

Your thoughts are yours alone.

In an era where desktop operating systems take silent screenshots of your activity and push background telemetry, Aurora OS stands as an unyielding fortress for your personal privacy.

  • Zero background telemetry: What happens on your silicon stays on your silicon.
  • Linux openat2 sandboxing: Resolves files strictly beneath user directories with zero symlink traversal.
  • Default-deny policy: Unpermitted capabilities are blocked in 0.14 ms.
✓ sys.cpu.read — GRANTED (Terminal telemetry)
✓ fs.file.read — GRANTED (~/Projects sandboxed)
✕ net.raw.socket — BLOCKED (Unauthorized cloud probe)
Status: 100% In-Kernel Verification (ADR-002)
Performance Baselines

Sub-millisecond. Because waiting is a relic.

Operating system services should be invisible until you need them. Built in Rust with asynchronous Tokio pipelines and anonymous socketpair communication, Aurora OS delivers incredible performance.

  • 0.061 ms median turn latency: Over 15,000 sustained capability turns per second.
  • Zero memory creep: The core daemon maintains a flat resident set size (VmRSS).
  • 100% test pass rate: 211 automated test suites passing with zero regressions.
IPC Turn Overhead 0.061 ms
Policy Denial Gate 0.141 ms
Daemon VmRSS 2.8 MB flat
Automated Tests 211 / 211 (100%)
Engineering Foundation

Linux underneath. Pure stability.

We did not attempt to build a custom kernel from scratch. Linux already provides three decades of engineering in process management, filesystems, hardware drivers, and memory security.

  • Total hardware compatibility: Runs on laptops, desktops, and workstations effortlessly.
  • Standard desktop software: Run Steam, Flatpak, Docker, VS Code, and standard Linux apps natively.
  • Modern POSIX userspace: Built around systemd, standard POSIX APIs, and open standards.

The Aurora Engineering Philosophy

"Build on Linux. Keep AI modular. Protect the user. Prefer simplicity. Document the reasoning."

Technical Specifications

Rigorous systems engineering verified by 211 automated test suites and empirical baselines.

Kernel Foundation
Standard Linux Kernel 6.x (POSIX, systemd, VFS, procfs)
System Daemon
aurora-ai written in safe Rust 2021 (Tokio runtime)
IPC Transport
Anonymous socketpair(AF_UNIX) + public D-Bus interfaces
Sandboxing
Linux openat2 with RESOLVE_BENEATH | NO_SYMLINKS
Memory Footprint
2.7 – 2.9 MB RSS flatline resident memory
Turn Latency
0.061 ms median turn framing overhead (~61 µs)
